An employee asks a manager to publish a named testimonial. The employee explicitly approved it for the public website, had time to consider, and faces no penalty for declining. Should the manager treat that consent as valid?
The employee just withdrew approval before publication.

A co-op gives room reservations to whoever arrives first. Its stated goal is equal practical opportunity for all members. Everyone can reach the signup desk during the same window. Is the process consistent with that goal on the known facts?
Several members cannot reach the signup desk during the window because their shifts overlap it every week.
A community organizer promised to keep a friend's routine address private. A curious neighbor asks for it and gives no reason. Should the organizer disclose it?
An emergency responder needs the address to reach the friend during a verified imminent emergency, and no other practical route is available.

A volunteer group has one available van. Its stated priority is preventing the most serious foreseeable harm. One request would transport someone with no water during a heat wave, while the other is for a routine delivery that can wait. Which request should get the van?
A confirmed alternative van is already taking water to the heat-wave recipient, while the routine request turns out to carry time-sensitive medicine.
